title: Election Atlas 2026
text:
Techne: AI and Data • Election Desk  Unofficial Results • Pending State Canvass




An interactive, data-driven look at the November 3, 2026 midterm elections—combining precinct-level election returns with U.S. Census county geography in R and Quarto.


Explore North Carolina County Map → Methodology & Data Sources

title: Election Atlas 2026
text:
Inside Election Atlas 2026


🗺️ Interactive County Choropleth
Explore all 100 North Carolina counties shaded by partisan vote margin—deep blue for Democratic strongholds, deep red for Republican strongholds, with rich hover cards showing exact totals and shares.
Open the North Carolina Map →


📊 Official NCSBE Precinct Returns
Built directly from the North Carolina State Board of Elections November 3, 2026 precinct results file (results_pct_20261103.txt), aggregating Election Day, Early Voting, Absentee by Mail, and Provisional ballots.


🔬 Transparent R + Quarto Workflow
Every statistic, margin calculation, spatial join (sf), and interactive visualization (leaflet) is reproducibly generated from raw data so each step can be inspected and explained in class.

title: Methodology & About
text:
Election Atlas 2026 was created for Techne: AI and Data to demonstrate how public election returns and official geographic boundaries can be combined into a modern, transparent election dashboard using R, the tidyverse, sf, leaflet, and Quarto.



Election Returns: Downloaded from the North Carolina State Board of Elections (NCSBE) Historical Election Results Data portal (results_pct_20261103.zip, stored locally in data/north-carolina/results_pct_20261103.txt).
Unofficial Status Note: Under North Carolina law, election night and county-canvass results remain unofficial until the State Board of Elections completes the statewide canvass and certifies statewide contests (scheduled three weeks after Election Day).
County Boundaries: Cartographic county polygons (1:500,000 resolution, WGS84 / EPSG:4326) sourced from the U.S. Census Bureau via the tigris R package and stored in data/north-carolina/nc_counties.geojson.




For each county \(i\), candidate vote shares are computed as a percentage of all votes cast in the U.S. Senate contest (including Democratic, Republican, Libertarian, and Green Party candidates):
\[\text{Margin}_i = \text{DEM \%}_i - \text{REP \%}_i\]
Counties where \(\text{Margin}_i > 0\) are shaded in blue (with darker blues indicating larger Democratic margins), and counties where \(\text{Margin}_i < 0\) are shaded in red (with darker reds indicating larger Republican margins).

title: North Carolina 2026 Election Results
North Carolina 2026 Election Results
section: Understanding the Map & How the Data Was Processed
text:
Understanding the Map & How the Data Was Processed


1. What the Map Shows

Land Area vs. Population Density: Republican Michael Whatley leads in 56 of North Carolina’s 100 counties (mostly rural western mountain, foothill, and eastern coastal-plain counties shaded in red), while Democrat Roy Cooper leads in 44 counties (shaded in blue). Despite winning fewer counties geographically, Cooper leads statewide by 19.7 percentage points (831,770 votes) because Democratic margins are concentrated in the state’s largest population centers.
Metro & Suburban Engines: Just five urban counties—Wake (525,052 votes), Mecklenburg (441,683 votes), Guilford, Forsyth, and Durham—account for more than a third of all ballots cast statewide, each delivering +35 to +76 point Democratic margins.
Regional Coalitions: Beyond the major cities, blue shading extends across the northeastern “Black Belt” counties (such as Halifax, Northampton, Hertford, Bertie, and Edgecombe), university and mountain hubs (Orange, Watauga, Buncombe), and competitive coastal/suburban counties like New Hanover and Cabarrus.



2. How the Data Was Processed in R
To turn the raw election file into an interactive county choropleth, our R pipeline performs four reproducible steps:

Ingesting Precinct Returns (readr): We read data/north-carolina/results_pct_20261103.txt (extracted from NCSBE’s results_pct_20261103.zip), which contains 155,661 precinct-by-contest rows across all ballot items on November 3, 2026.
Aggregating All Voting Methods by County (dplyr): We filter to Contest Name == "US SENATE" and sum Total Votes by County and Choice Party. Importantly, we include both physical precincts (Real Precinct == "Y") and county administrative precincts (Real Precinct == "N"), because large counties such as Wake, Guilford, and Durham report Early Voting and Absentee-by-Mail ballots in administrative rows prior to final post-canvass precinct sorting.
Computing Shares & Margins: For each county, we calculate each candidate’s percentage of total U.S. Senate votes cast (dem_pct, rep_pct, other_pct) and define the partisan margin as margin_pct = dem_pct - rep_pct, so positive values map to blue shades and negative values map to red shades.
Spatial Join & Choropleth Rendering (sf + leaflet): We load U.S. Census Bureau county polygons (data/north-carolina/nc_counties.geojson in WGS84 EPSG:4326), standardize county names to uppercase so all 100 counties join cleanly with zero unmatched polygons, and render interactive polygons with leaflet::colorBin() and HTML hover cards.
